text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Paul Bernardo's ex-lawyers charged: Two removed damning tapes from house the day before Homolka struck plea bargain.
- Cities' credit ratings at risk: Business allies decry Tory plan.
- Hong Kong's future leader stirs up furor: Tung defends China's intention to roll back civil-liberties measures.
- Ontario government kept tabs on callers: Manual for information hot line ordered detailed reports on identity of dissenters, supporters.
- Forest firms sprout red ink: Domtar, Avenor aand Tembec post losses in quarter as paper market fails to rebound.
- IBM Canada beats parent in drive to refocus business: Leads in making services the core element of sales.
- B.C. shuts down smelter talks with Alcan: Government demands that firm cancel lawsuit before resuming negotiations.
- Placer wins bid for Highlands mine: C$250-million for prized gold property.
- Investors scan correction radar as stocks dive.
- Pepsi food-chain spinoff may open doors for Scott's.
- Cuba agrees to talks on compensating Canadian insurers.
